title: Misleading id literals in tests: chat-missing never asserted, react-ulid-1 isn't a ULID
description:
Two cases of identifier strings that misrepresent their purpose:

1. chat_smoke_tests.rs:119 — `let ids = [Id::from("chat-1"), Id::from("chat-missing")];` The second id name only makes sense if the test asserted on notFound. The test never asserts on resp.not_found. Either add the notFound assertion (preferable — it's the test's stated intent per the name) or rename the literal.

2. message_smoke_tests.rs:478 message_update_reaction_add_uses_json_pointer_patch_key uses sender_reaction_id: "react-ulid-1". A ULID is a 26-character Crockford-base32 string; this string is neither. If the chat draft or production code imposes ULID-shape validation, this test wouldn't catch a regression on that. If it doesn't, the literal name misleads readers. Rename to e.g. "react-1" or use a real ULID like "01H7XKJZQ8N5A2BCDEFGHIJKMN".
